The derivative and modulus are correct: $f'(\theta)=ie^{i\theta}(1+e^{i\theta})^2$ gives $|f'(\theta)|=2+2\cos\theta$. The self-intersection is unique: the condition $z_1+z_2+\tfrac{z_1^2+z_1z_2+z_2^2}{3}=-1$ for distinct unit-circle points forces the pair $\{e^{2\pi i/3}, e^{4\pi i/3}\}$, with $f=-\tfrac{2}{3}$. The turning number of the tangent is $\frac{1}{2\pi}\cdot 4\pi=2$, so the two loops have the same orientation and the inner loop sits inside the outer one. The boundary of $R$ is therefore the outer loop.

The outer loop's length is $2\int_0^{2\pi/3}(2+2\cos\theta)\,d\theta = 2\left(\tfrac{4\pi}{3}+\sqrt3\right)=\tfrac{8\pi}{3}+2\sqrt3\approx 11.841682$, which matches the given numerical value. The check that inner plus outer lengths sum to $4\pi$ also holds.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
CONFIDENCE: 4
